title: The Roman Senate and the Consuls
lead: The Roman Senate still met under the emperors, passed decrees, tried cases and flattered. Two consuls were named each year and gave the year its name; Tacitus opens by dating the work to the year Galba was consul for the second time (Histories of Tacitus 1:1).

sections.b: Wikipedia says Augustus cut the Senate from 900 to 600, that its decrees had the force of law (mainly in finance and administration), and that it held criminal trials with a consul presiding. Two consuls were chosen each year and Romans dated years by the two consuls in office; under the emperors the emperor in practice named them, and more than two could serve in a year. Former consuls governed the largest provinces. Tacitus shows the Senate in 69 as a body that votes Otho every imperial honor on the day Galba dies (1:47) and spends its debates in fear and flattery (1:85). Compare Luke 3:1, which dates the start of John's work by the emperor's year and the local rulers, not by consuls.
